> The operational examples assume that the SSPICE project root is the working directory. They are displayed but not run when the vignette is built because they require project data.

# Why SSPICE?

SSPICE represents questionnaire dependencies as a directed acyclic graph (DAG). It uses the graph to check routing, locate inconsistencies, construct variable domains and formal rules, correct inconsistent records, and assess correction outcomes. Missing values are meaningful: an inactive question must be blank, whereas an active question may require a response.

# Workflow

```text
Routing metadata ──> canonical DAG ───────────────────┐
                          │                            │
Data + external sources ──> prepared data ──> checks   │
                          │                  │         │
                          └──> logical edits ──> extended DAG
                                                  │
                                    correction <──┘
                                        │
                                   quality report

Canonical DAG ──> VARDOM / RULES ──> Horn validation
```

The operational steps are in `scripts/`: `00_config.R` specifies paths and options; `01_build_DAG.R` builds the graph; `02_prepare_data.R` prepares records; `03_run_routing_check.R` checks routing; `04_create_VARDOM_and_RULES.R` generates constraints; `05_validate_horn_theory.R` and `06_validate_violation_localization.R` assess their properties; and `09_build_extended_DAG.R`, `10_correct_data.R`, and `11_correction_quality_report.R` perform correction and evaluation. Scripts 07 and 08 generate synthetic data and count admissible patterns, respectively.

```{r workflow}
source(file.path("scripts", "00_config.R"))
source(file.path("scripts", "01_build_DAG.R"))
source(file.path("scripts", "02_prepare_data.R"))
source(file.path("scripts", "03_run_routing_check.R"))
```

Run the steps in order and inspect intermediate outputs before starting correction. Diagnostic quality depends on the quality of the metadata.
